The rfb rule, step by step

Source: vignettes/rfb-rule.Rmd
rfb-rule.Rmd

The rfb rule (ICES 2025, method 2.1) sets the catch advice of a category 3 stock with slow growth (von Bertalanffy K < 0.32) from a biomass index and the length distribution of the catch:

Ay+1=Ay×r×f×b×mA_{y+1} = A_y \times r \times f \times b \times m

  • rr: the index ratio, the mean of the last two index values over the mean of the three before them;
  • ff: the fishing pressure proxy, the mean length of the catch above Lc over the target length LF=M = 0.75 Lc + 0.25 Linf;
  • bb: the biomass safeguard, min(1, Ilast / Itrigger), with Itrigger = 1.4 Iloss;
  • mm: the precautionary multiplier (0.95 for K < 0.2, 0.9 for 0.2 ≤ K < 0.32);

followed by the stability clause (the advice changes by at most +20% / −30%, unless b<1b < 1).

The MFRI rfb stocks run it in their targets pipelines: 13-cas, 14-mon, 24-lem, 25-wit, 26-meg, 27-dab and 60-norway-redfish. This vignette goes through the same steps on simulated data. The numbers are made up and belong to no stock.

library(dlsrules)

Simulated data

The pipelines keep the survey indices as one long table, one row per index series and year, with biomass b, abundance n and their CVs. In the stock repos it is built with pax::pax_si_length_index() from the spring survey, and the series names say which length range they cover (e.g. smb_harv, the biomass of fish over 30 cm in 25-wit).

set.seed(1)
years <- 1985:2025
b <- round(2000 * exp(cumsum(c(0, rnorm(length(years) - 1, 0, 0.15)))))
survey_index <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    index = "smb_harv", year = years, b = b,
    b_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.12, 0.3), 2),
    n = round(b / 0.6), n_cv = 0.2
  ),
  data.frame(
    index = "smb_rec", year = years, b = round(b / 5), b_cv = 0.3,
    n = round(rlnorm(length(years), log(1500), 0.4)),
    n_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.2, 0.4), 2)
  )
)
tail(survey_index[survey_index$index == "smb_harv", ], 6)
#>       index year    b b_cv    n n_cv
#> 36 smb_harv 2020 2993 0.12 4988  0.2
#> 37 smb_harv 2021 2812 0.25 4687  0.2
#> 38 smb_harv 2022 2650 0.14 4417  0.2
#> 39 smb_harv 2023 2627 0.20 4378  0.2
#> 40 smb_harv 2024 3098 0.24 5163  0.2
#> 41 smb_harv 2025 3474 0.30 5790  0.2

The catch length distribution: numbers by year and 1 cm length class.

z <- 0.12 + 0.05 * sin(seq_along(1990:2024) / 4)
ldist <- expand.grid(length = 20:70, year = 1990:2024)
ldist$n <- round(
  2000 * plogis((ldist$length - 32) / 1.5) *
    exp(-z[ldist$year - 1989] * (ldist$length - 32) / 1.2 * (ldist$length > 32))
)
ldist <- ldist[, c("year", "length", "n")]
head(ldist[ldist$year == 2024 & ldist$length >= 30, ])
#>      year length    n
#> 1745 2024     30  417
#> 1746 2024     31  678
#> 1747 2024     32 1000
#> 1748 2024     33 1165
#> 1749 2024     34 1230
#> 1750 2024     35 1207

The catch length distribution from a pax database

In a stock repo the length distribution comes from the pax_db target with catch_ldist(). The ldist table that pax::pax_from_mar() builds is already raised to the counted fish at import, so catch_ldist() only rounds the lengths (pax::pax_ldist_scale_round()) and does not raise the counts a second time. Building the distribution with pax::pax_ldist_by_year() and its default scaling raises twice: the length distributions of single years are then a few percent too high in samples with counted fish (found in the 04-whg port).

A toy database with two samples shows the call (pax is in Suggests, and only catch_ldist() needs it):

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "station", data.frame(
  sample_id = 1:3,
  sampling_type = c(1, 8, 30), # two commercial samples, one survey tow
  year = 2024,
  mfdb_gear_code = c("BMT", "DSE", "BMT")
))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "ldist", data.frame(
  sample_id = c(1, 1, 2, 3),
  species = 25, sex = NA_integer_,
  length = c(35.4, 40.6, 41, 30),
  count = c(3, 2, 5, 100)
))
catch_ldist(
  dplyr::tbl(con, "station"),
  dplyr::tbl(con, "ldist"),
  gears = c("BMT", "DSE", "NPT"),
  year_start = 1976
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>    year length     n
#>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  2024     35     3
#> 2  2024     41     7
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

The survey tow (sampling type 30) is left out; the defaults are the commercial samples at sea and in port (1, 2, 8). The gears and the first year are stock choices (25-wit: bottom trawl, Danish seine and Nephrops trawl from 1976; 60-norway-redfish: bottom trawl from 1997). With by_gear = TRUE the gear is kept, and rule_ldist() selects from the collected table later (see vignette("stock-choices")).

The components

Index ratio, r

index_series() picks one series from the long table, in the form the rules take (year, index). Cut it at the assessment year: the ratio uses the last five rows it is given.

assessment_year <- 2025
index <- index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv", year_end = assessment_year)
calc_ratio(index, num = 2, den = 3)
#>        Component       value
#> IndexA    IndexA 3286.000000
#> IndexB    IndexB 2696.333333
#> ratio      ratio    1.218692

Fishing pressure proxy, f

LF=M comes from Lc and Linf. The rule uses the mean length above Lc (strictly above) in the year before the assessment year (lag = 1): the catch sampling of the assessment year is not complete when the advice is given.

Lc <- 33
Linf <- 0.9 * 69 # 25-wit: 0.9 x the largest length in the catch
target_reference_length(Lc = Lc, Linf = Linf)
#> [1] 40.275
mean_length_above(ldist[ldist$year == assessment_year - 1, ], Lc = Lc)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>    year mean_length
#>   <int>       <dbl>
#> 1  2024        41.4
fishing_pressure_proxy(ldist, Linf = Linf, Lc = Lc,
                       assessment_year = assessment_year, lag = 1)$fpp
#> [1] 1.028187

If the length data has no rows for assessment_year - lag, f is NaN and so is the advice. Check that the last year of the catch distribution is the year you expect.

Iloss, Itrigger and the biomass safeguard, b

Iloss has no default: ICES (2025) says the lowest observed index value, but the stocks differ (vignette("stock-choices")). calc_iloss() gives it, and ref_points_iloss() adds I_lim (= Iloss), I_lim_year and I_trigger to the list of reference points.

calc_iloss(index, method = "min")
#> $I_loss
#> [1] 1651
#> 
#> $year
#> [1] 1988
ref_points <- list(K = 0.147, Linf = Linf, Lc = Lc, F_msy_proxy = 1)
ref_points <- ref_points_iloss(ref_points, index, method = "min")
str(ref_points)
#> List of 7
#>  $ K          : num 0.147
#>  $ Linf       : num 62.1
#>  $ Lc         : num 33
#>  $ F_msy_proxy: num 1
#>  $ I_lim      : num 1651
#>  $ I_lim_year : int 1988
#>  $ I_trigger  : num 2311
biomass_safeguard(
  Inow = index$index[index$year == assessment_year],
  Itrigger = ref_points$I_trigger
)
#> [1] 1

Always pass I_trigger this way. If ref_points has neither I_trigger nor I_lim, rfb_rule() falls back on 1.4 × the lowest value of the index it is given and only says so with cat().

Multiplier, m, and the stability clause 

multiplier_lookup(ref_points$K)
#> [1] 0.95
stability_clause(tac = 2500, prev_tac = 1659, bsg = 1) # capped at +20%
#> [1] 1990.8
stability_clause(tac = 900, prev_tac = 1659, bsg = 1)  # capped at -30%
#> [1] 1161.3
stability_clause(tac = 900, prev_tac = 1659, bsg = 0.8) # not applied when b < 1
#> [1] 900

The advice: rfb_advice()

rfb_advice() cuts the index at the assessment year, runs rfb_rule() and returns the components with lower-case names and the assessment year. This is the rfb_prognosis target of the stock repos.

prognosis <- rfb_advice(
  index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv"),
  ldist,
  ref_points = ref_points,
  prev_tac = 1659,
  assessment_year = assessment_year
)
prognosis
#> # A tibble: 17 × 4
#>    component                   value type                     assessment_year
#>    <chr>                       <dbl> <chr>                              <dbl>
#>  1 previous_catch_advice    1659     advice                              2025
#>  2 index_A                  3286     stock_biomass_trend                 2025
#>  3 index_B                  2696     stock_biomass_trend                 2025
#>  4 index_ratio                 1.22  stock_biomass_trend                 2025
#>  5 mean_catch_length          41.4   fishing_pressure_proxy              2025
#>  6 msy_proxy_length           40.3   fishing_pressure_proxy              2025
#>  7 fpp_ratio                   1.03  fishing_pressure_proxy              2025
#>  8 fpp_ratio_inv               0.973 fishing_pressure_proxy              2025
#>  9 last_index_value         3474     biomass_safeguard                   2025
#> 10 Itrigger                 2311     biomass_safeguard                   2025
#> 11 Iloss                    1651     biomass_safeguard                   2025
#> 12 biomass_safeguard           1     biomass_safeguard                   2025
#> 13 multiplier                  0.95  precautionary_multiplier            2025
#> 14 initial_catch_advice     1975.    advice                              2025
#> 15 stability_clause_applied    0     advice                              2025
#> 16 catch_advice             1975.    advice                              2025
#> 17 advice_change              19     advice                              2025

The product of the components gives the initial advice:

v <- setNames(prognosis$value, prognosis$component)
v[["previous_catch_advice"]] * v[["index_ratio"]] * v[["fpp_ratio"]] *
  v[["biomass_safeguard"]] * v[["multiplier"]]
#> [1] 1974.859
v[["initial_catch_advice"]]
#> [1] 1974.859

index_A, index_B and the I values are rounded in the table; the advice is computed from the unrounded values.

In the stock repos the prognosis feeds hafroreports::hr_advice_table_rfb() (the advice sheet table) and the rfb figures of the tech report, and advice_hist_rows() (vignette("history-tables")).

Pitfalls

  • Double raising: use catch_ldist() (or pax::pax_ldist_scale_round() as its ldist_tbl) for the length distribution. The pax ldist table is already raised.
  • Index past the assessment year: a later year in the index shifts index_A and index_B. rfb_advice() cuts it, rfb_rule() does not.
  • K: rfb_rule() stops for K ≥ 0.32. Use the chr rule (vignette("chr-rule")) for 0.32 ≤ K < 0.45.
  • Lc and Linf are fixed between benchmarks in the stock’s config.R. Don’t re-estimate them in each run: they change LF=M, f and the F proxy series of the history table.
  • The previous advice is the advice for the fishing year that starts in the assessment year minus one, read from data/advice_hist.csv. For a biennial advice this is the second year of the previous advice (vignette("stock-choices")).
